name: Jar
dimensions: Diameter of mouth: 12.8 cm (5 1/16 in.); Overall: 25.7 cm (10 1/8 in.)
summary: Bronze Age potters customarily used patterned wooden paddles to smooth the ridges of their coil-built wares. Because such early pots were beaten repeatedly and randomly while still in the leather-hard state, the paddles did not leave isolated, self-contained patterns, but an overall surface texture.
